**Finding submitted: deviation (medium severity, term-termination).**

**What the document says.** Section 4.1 (¶ p0024) sets a one-year initial term from the Effective Date, with automatic successive one-year renewals on each anniversary, terminable by either party only on **ninety (90) days' written notice**.

**Analysis against RENEWAL:**

| Element | Document | Playbook | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Renewal term length | 12 months | 12 months | ✔ Compliant |
| Non-renewal notice window | 90 days | ≤ 30 preferred / ≤ 60 fallback | �’ **Fails fallback** |
| Renewal price uplift | No repricing language (fees run off Net Sales) | ≤ CPI/3 % pref., ≤ 5 % fallback | ✔ Not engaged |
| Vendor renewal reminder | None | 60-day reminder (preferred) | Minor sub-element, noted only |

The 90-day window is the sole material failure. It is not walk-away territory — walk-away requires a window *longer than* 90 days or automatic *multi-year* renewals, and neither applies here, since renewals are annual and the window sits exactly at the 90-day line. But it clearly exceeds the 60-day fallback ceiling, so it cannot be left unredlined.

**Redline (validated ok:true).** Single minimal edit reaching the preferred position: "ninety (90)" → "thirty (30)". I deliberately did not restructure the clause, add a reminder mechanic, or insert a price cap — the term length is already at 12 months and there is no uplift language to cap, so anything further would be gratuitous.

**One point worth flagging for the negotiation.** The notice right in 4.1 is bilateral, so shortening it also lets HDI exit faster. Two mitigating factors made the straight shortening the right call: the playbook's redline guidance is unqualified on this point, and Section 4.2 imposes a Termination Payment on the Company (Net Sales for the preceding twelve months less $800,000, halved) when *we* terminate — meaning our exit is the expensive one, and a long notice window compounds that friction rather than protecting us. If HDI resists on the grounds of symmetry, the fallback landing spot is a 60-day window, which still clears the playbook. Note that the Termination Payment itself is a separate commercial term and I have not flagged it under this rule.
